market.structuralNote: Government's RDSS (Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme) is the policy driver; trade press frames this as a '₹2 lakh crore opportunity' / '₹1.3 lakh crore AMI revolution' behind a 25-crore-meter installation push nationally.
market.domesticSlice: figures are India-specific; policy (RDSS) driven, not an export story for the India entity

structureFacts: The AMISP (Advanced Metering Infrastructure Service Provider) model is annuity-like: providers collect recurring monthly fees per meter for the lifetime of the deployment, with contracts often spanning a decade — a structurally different revenue pattern from a one-time equipment sale.
India's smart-meter installation push targets roughly 25 crore (250 million) meters nationally, under the RDSS scheme.

adoptionStructure.note: Demand is driven by state utility tenders under RDSS, awarded via the DBFOOT (Design-Build-Finance-Own-Operate-Transfer) model — a government/utility-tender-driven market, not consumer-facing demand.

peers.name: Genus Power Infrastructures
peers.note: The dominant incumbent: 80M+ meters deployed lifetime, an executable order book of ~₹27,217 Cr covering ~2.75 crore smart meters (2.5 crore already supplied), commanding ~45% market share of installed units. Operates as an AMISP under the DBFOOT model.

peers.name: HPL Electric & Power
peers.note: Order book ~₹3,100 Cr, over 99% from smart metering projects.

peers.name: Secure Meters Ltd
peers.note: Specializes in RF mesh/NB-IoT technology; operates as an AMISP in Madhya Pradesh and other states.

drivers: Winning state utility tenders under RDSS — the primary demand-generation mechanism.
AMISP financing/operational capability (DBFOOT model) — providers effectively finance and operate the metering infrastructure, not just sell hardware.
Technology fit (RF mesh, NB-IoT, prepayment, group metering) for the specific utility's grid characteristics.
customerValue.strongestPredictor: Order-book size and tender win-rate under RDSS — the segment's real scoreboard, led decisively by Genus Power's ~45% installed-unit share.

steps: identify state utility tender under RDSS
operate AMISP financing and data-management platforms
maintain field service and O&M capability
plan production against awarded tender volumes
operate/maintain meters over the contract term (often a decade)
demand arises from state RDSS rollout schedules
recurring revenue over the multi-year AMISP term

sources: IMARC Group, Astute Analytica, TechSci Research (India smart meter/AMI market sizing)
CIOnLabs, NES India (RDSS policy context, ₹ lakh-crore opportunity framing)
Genus Power Infrastructures' own site, TradeBrains (peer order books/market share)
